problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate the municipal budget across 14 different infrastructure projects to maximize the overall community benefit score.
The profile for each project is as follows:
* Project A: benefit score 0.091, impact factor 0.215, allocation bounds [0.016, 0.599]
* Project B: benefit score 0.078, impact factor 0.194, allocation bounds [0.014, 0.599]
* Project C: benefit score 0.024, impact factor 0.035, allocation bounds [0.077, 0.784]
* Project D: benefit score 0.102, impact factor 0.215, allocation bounds [0.005, 0.665]
* Project E: benefit score 0.181, impact factor 0.221, allocation bounds [0.031, 0.596]
* Project F: benefit score 0.181, impact factor 0.293, allocation bounds [0.073, 0.430]
* Project G: benefit score 0.179, impact factor 0.188, allocation bounds [0.096, 0.696]
* Project H: benefit score 0.036, impact factor 0.056, allocation bounds [0.029, 0.572]
* Project I: benefit score 0.078, impact factor 0.170, allocation bounds [0.018, 0.565]
* Project J: benefit score 0.137, impact factor 0.023, allocation bounds [0.090, 0.661]
* Project K: benefit score 0.148, impact factor 0.060, allocation bounds [0.096, 0.304]
* Project L: benefit score 0.050, impact factor 0.107, allocation bounds [0.000, 0.829]
* Project M: benefit score 0.152, impact factor 0.263, allocation bounds [0.077, 0.467]
* Project N: benefit score 0.036, impact factor 0.260, allocation bounds [0.001, 0.677]
Each project must receive a portion of the total budget that falls within its specified lower and upper bounds, and the sum of all budget portions must equal the entire budget. To ensure rapid implementation, the planner requires that the group of quick-delivery projects, represented by the subset Q = {J, K, L, M, N}, collectively receive at least 0.515 of the total funding. Furthermore, the overall portfolio impact, measured by a composite impact index, must not exceed 0.168, and the total community benefit score must be no less than 0.084. Please determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total community benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
